title: Implement synthetic permissioned probes and metadata-enriched breadcrumbs for analytics ingest debugging
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Background: We frequently see production ingest regressions that are hard to reproduce because customer traffic is noisy and tenant-localized. Existing synthetic probes exercise only top-level API liveness and do not carry tenant-scoped metadata so traces and logs produced by probes are not directly comparable to user traffic.
Scope: Build a small fleet of permissioned synthetic probes that run as first-class tenants to exercise the analytics ingest pipeline end-to-end (ingest front-end, routing, batching, KV cache, model routing, and async storage). Probes must carry a structured metadata header that is propagated into traces, log breadcrumbs, and cost-metrics so that probe runs are queryable and correlated with backend processing.
Goals: 1) Detect regressions earlier with tenant-like traffic patterns; 2) Improve debugging speed by having probe runs attached to full traces, enriched logs, and a small set of KPIs; 3) Provide a retrospective cost bucket per-probe run to correlate regressions with cost anomalies.
Approach:
- Probe orchestration service will create ephemeral API keys scoped to a "probe" tenant and rotate them daily.
- Each probe run attaches a metadata object (probe_id, probe_tier, synthetic_user_id, target_route, batch_window_ms, expected_cache_hit_bool, model_variant_hint). This metadata is injected into trace tags and log fields (not payload) and included in the ingestion event headers.
- Tracing: ensure trace sampling logic preserves probe spans even under adaptive sampling; add a probe-trace flag to the trace header to force retention when needed.
- Logging: add breadcrumb lines at each major processing stage (received, routed, batched, kv_cache_lookup, model_exec_start, model_exec_end, persisted) with the probe metadata and small structured context for quick grep and live tailing.
- Metrics: emit probe_run_duration_ms, probe_success{0|1}, probe_kv_cache_hit_ratio, probe_batch_size_distribution, probe_cost_estimate_usd for each run.
- Dashboards: new dashboards with probe health panel, heatmap of latency vs batch_size, and retrospective cost per run.
- Runbook changes: add a dedicated playbook section to use probe IDs to locate traces, logs, and cost breakdowns for postmortems.
acceptance_criteria: A fleet of at least 5 probes deployed across regions with daily rotations and documented keys
Probe metadata is present on traces and logs and queryable in the console (example filter: probe_id:synthetic-42)
Dashboards show probe SLI panels: probe_success_rate (30d), p50/p95 probe latency, probe_cost_estimate_usd per run
Probe traces are retained independent of adaptive sampling when flag is set and links to raw event logs are available from trace view
Runbook sections updated with exact queries and escalation steps using probe identifiers
No customer PII or customer tenant identifiers are used in probe metadata; probes must be flagged as synthetic in telemetry ingestion
